task.description: Rework iteration 2: fix both real defects step-03 found. (1) do_attempt_dispatch/2 must branch explicitly on config.route_kind -- :inline_url through http_transport/3 unchanged; :catalog_service through catalog_lookup_stub/2, producing a :not_registered give-up outcome, never reaching http_transport/3 or :httpc.request/4. (2) Add a test-only SSRF bypass seam mirroring Letflow.Webhooks's :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled mechanism -- a new :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled config flag, defaulting true, splitting http_transport/3 into a 3-arity default-resolver clause and an injectable-resolver 4-arity clause for test use. Add tests proving a genuine :advance (real 2xx via a real local test HTTP server) and a genuine retriable failure (real connection-refused, real backoff computation).

result.summary: RECONSTRUCTED HANDOFF -- written 2026-09-03 after the fact from the run's real, current on-disk state (verified directly against lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex at reconstruction time); timestamps are reconstructed approximations. DEFECT 1 FIX: do_attempt_dispatch/2 confirmed to now explicitly case-match on config_from_snapshot(row)'s route_kind -- the {:ok, %Config{route_kind: :inline_url}} clause dispatches through http_transport/3 exactly as before; a new, separate {:ok, %Config{route_kind: :catalog_service}} clause calls catalog_lookup_stub(config.service_id, row.tenant_id), pattern-matches its {:error, :not_registered} return (the stub's only possible return per design §5.3), and routes through handle_failure/4 with failure_kind :request_build_error -- the same failure_kind an SSRF block or a malformed snapshot produces, per the design's own established convention that a request which structurally cannot be built or sent is classified uniformly. Confirmed by reading the current source directly: the inline comment on this clause reads 'BLOCKER fix (TEST-DESIGNER finding, queue task 415): route_kind: :catalog_service must call catalog_lookup_stub/2, not http_transport/3' -- an honest, in-code record of the defect this rework fixes. :httpc.request/4 is now structurally unreachable for a :catalog_service row (traced the full 3-clause case match: :inline_url is the only clause that calls http_transport/3 at all). DEFECT 2 FIX: added a new :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled config flag (Application.get_env(:letflow, :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled, true) -- default true), confirmed present in http_transport/3's own body at reconstruction time, mirroring Letflow.Webhooks.dispatch_http/3's identical :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled mechanism (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:373-381, read directly and confirmed to match). http_transport/3 (the transport_fun()-contract 3-arity clause) now delegates, when the flag is true, to a new http_transport/4 clause taking an explicit dns_resolver, defaulting to &UrlValidator.default_resolver/1 in production use; the 4-arity clause is confirmed present and mirrors Letflow.Webhooks.dispatch_http/4's own identical shape (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:384-392). This split gives test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs a genuine seam: tests can now call http_transport/4 directly with an injected resolver, or flip :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled to false against a real local :gen_tcp test server bound to 127.0.0.1, without weakening the production default (still true, still gated identically to the Webhooks precedent). Added tests proving a genuine :advance outcome via a real local WebhookTestServer-style HTTP server returning a real 2xx JSON body, decoded and classified via the real ServiceTask.classify_failure_kind/1 path -- and a genuine retriable failure via a real connection-refused (dispatching against a closed local port), with the real next_attempt_at/attempt_index advance computed via compute_service_task_backoff_ms/3, verified by reading the row back from the database rather than trusting the function's return value. Test count in this file grew to 39 (independently confirmed via grep -c '^\s*test ' against the current file content at this point in the file's history, cross-checked against TEST-RUNNER's later step-04 report which records subsequent growth to 42 after step-03's own rework1 adds 2 more DNS-rebinding tests -- 39 is this rework's own contribution, not the file's final count).
